answer: Divergent-secret challenge protocol. Each identity must publish a whisper of a random secret, then answer a challenge derived from other identities' secrets; a clone answering identically reveals the shared source, so the quill signing its response must commit to a fresh divergent value or forfeit. An attacker cloning N agents pays N distinct secret-generation and signing costs plus a velvet penalty escrow per identity that is slashed on any detectable correlation, making mass cloning linearly expensive rather than free.
